whatItIs.statement: A governed native text link with permanent underline, semantic primary color, inherited typography and inline wrapping.

whenToUse.statement: Use Link for navigation embedded in prose, descriptions or ordinary text. Use Button for actions; existing Breadcrumb, Pagination and Sidebar navigation components continue to own their respective structures.

whenNotToUse.statement: Do not use Link to trigger an action or represent a disabled action. Link requires a real destination and meaningful content; application routing, current-page state and navigation interception remain consumer-owned.

howToUse.statement: Supply href and meaningful children, for example <Link href="/docs">Documentation</Link>. Internal paths, external URLs, hash destinations, mailto and tel destinations all use native anchor behavior without origin or scheme detection.

Required children provide the native accessible name. The runtime rejects plainly empty arrays, null, booleans and whitespace-only strings; opaque child elements remain the author’s responsibility for meaningful accessible naming. Required href must be a non-empty string at runtime. These runtime refinements exceed the structural string and ReactNode authoring types.

Use newTab=true only when deliberately opening a new tab. Link owns target=_blank and rel=noopener; include a phrase such as “opens in a new tab” in child content when helpful. An external destination alone does not imply newTab.

options.statement: The closed API consists of href, children and newTab=false. There is no className, style, role, ref, asChild, disabled, target, rel, extra metadata or event-handler passthrough.

Link remains inline and inherits the surrounding font, text size, wrapping and reading direction in light, dark and RTL contexts. Its permanent underline identifies navigation; keyboard focus uses the semantic ring and background offset.
